title: Shipment dispatcher and its test fakes
name: Shipment label dispatcher

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these tests use fakes to isolate the dispatcher (clock, repository, carrier)? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does InMemoryShipmentRepo return copies ({ ...r }) from get and store copies in save?
choices: To make the fake faster than a Map lookup
So the test only passes if the dispatcher actually calls save, mirroring a real database that does not share object references
Because TypeScript requires spread to satisfy the Shipment interface
To prevent the carrier fake from seeing the tracking number

questions.prompt: The second test uses 2024-03-31T17:00:00Z. What does it verify about pickupDateFor?
choices: That 17:00 exactly is before the cutoff, so pickup stays on 03-31
That local server time zone is used
That reaching the cutoff hour rolls to the next day, including across a month boundary
That the carrier rejects past dates

questions.prompt: What would most likely happen to the cutoff tests if ShipmentDispatcher called new Date() directly instead of this.clock.now()?
choices: They would pass or fail depending on when the suite runs
They would still be deterministic because FixedClock is passed in
They would always pass because the pickup date is computed from the shipment
